title: Kestrel Commercial Fleet Lease Master Agreement: Termination Notice, Turn-In and End-of-Lease Charges
content:
# Master Lease Agreement — Termination and Turn-In Clause, Kestrel Commercial Fleet Lease

## Clause T1 — Notice

A termination notice takes effect only when a named authorized signer has completed the termination notice request for the unit. The evidence is the system record of that request for that unit.

## Clause T2 — Earliest turn-in

The unit may be turned in no earlier than the termination notice period (in calendar days) after the termination notice was received. The notice period is counted in calendar days starting the day after the termination notice date recorded on the unit, and turn-in on the last day of the period is permitted.

| Element | Rule |
|---|---|
| Clock starts | the termination notice date on the unit |
| Counting | calendar days, the first counted day being the day after the notice date |
| Comparison | turn-in no earlier than the last day of the notice period |
| Last day itself | permitted |

**Boundary cases (hypothetical, notice period of 30 calendar days, notice dated day 0):** turn-in on day 29 is too early; turn-in on day 30 is permitted.

## Clause T3 — Lapse and withdrawal

A notice lapses, and the unit returns to in service, when the unit is not turned in within the turn-in limit in calendar days after the notice date; the business may withdraw a notice before turn-in.

## Clause T4 — TRAC minimum-term charge

A TRAC unit turned in while its months short of the minimum term are above zero is billed a minimum-term charge equal to its monthly depreciation amount multiplied by those months. The months short of the minimum term are the minimum term in months less the unit's months in service at the turn-in date, never below zero; the monthly depreciation amount is the capitalized cost multiplied by the monthly depreciation percentage, divided by 100 and rounded to the nearest cent, before it is multiplied.

**Worked example (hypothetical):** a TRAC unit with a capitalized cost of 36000 and a monthly depreciation percentage of 2.25, turned in after 9 months in service against a 12-month minimum term, is 3 months short. Its monthly depreciation amount is 810.00, and the minimum-term charge is 810.00 multiplied by 3, that is 2430.00. The same unit turned in after 12 or more months in service is not short, and no minimum-term charge arises.

## Clause T5 — Closed-end commercial units

(a) *No longer in force:* the clause "A closed-end commercial unit ended before its scheduled end date is billed the closed-end early termination fee" is no longer in force as written here; it has been superseded by the current basis for early termination charges on closed-end units.

(b) *No longer in force:* the clause "at any end it is billed excess mileage at the closed-end excess mileage rate for its vehicle class for miles above the annual mileage allowance multiplied by the months in service and divided by 12" is no longer in force as written here; it has been superseded by the current basis for excess mileage charges on closed-end units.

(c) At any end, a closed-end commercial unit is billed wear charges capped at the tier's wear-charge cap percentage of its capitalized cost. This part of the clause remains in force.

## Clause T6 — Rentals through turn-in

Rentals continue to be invoiced through the month of turn-in.
